key_insight: The paper proposes a first-quantized quantum simulation framework that uses a finite grid spacing to derive a generalized uncertainty principle, revealing different low- and high-energy behaviors and a possible minimum length scale.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum computing engineers a route to model quantum-gravity-inspired dynamics on qubit hardware, especially for exploring relativistic and high-energy regimes beyond standard continuum assumptions.
method: Encode 1D quantum systems in first quantization using L qubits.
Introduce a finite-difference grid with minimum spacing ΔL and derive the GUP analytically.
Analyze low-energy and high-energy momentum formulations, including cases matched to special-relativistic and HUP-consistent behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytic derivation and regime analysis, showing recovery of the HUP in the low-energy limit and distinct high-energy predictions under different consistency assumptions.
watch_item: The approach depends on the chosen discretization and momentum-matching assumptions, so physical conclusions about minimum length and relativistic consistency may be model-dependent.
paper_title: Quantum Gravity Simulation: Quantum simulation with a minimum length based on the generalised uncertainty principle
